T: One step. One punch. One cheesesteak.
D: Apollo Creed's son asks Rocky to train him and steps out of his father's shadow.
P: Serve the mains when Adonis and Bianca go out for cheesesteaks.
S: the Italian restaurant Rocky runs, named after Adrian
Salami and provolone folded on a board with olives warmed in olive oil, marinated artichokes, strips of roasted capsicum and torn crusty bread.
Italian hoagie bites with hot peppers

Long rolls layered with ham, salami, capocollo, provolone, lettuce, tomato and onion, dressed with oil, vinegar and oregano, cut into bites with hot cherry peppers. Split 2 long Italian rolls. Drizzle the insides with olive oil and red wine vinegar and sprinkle with dried oregano. Layer with 100g leg ham, 100g salami, 100g capocollo and 100g provolone. Top with shredded iceberg, sliced tomato, thin red onion and chopped hot cherry peppers. Press closed, wrap tightly for 15 minutes, then cut each into 6 bites with a toothpick through each.
the old boxing gym in Philly
Medjool dates, oats, peanut butter, cocoa and a pinch of salt blitzed in a food processor, rolled into balls and coated in desiccated coconut, chilled an hour.
M: Rib eye frozen 30 minutes, shaved thin, seared on a hot plate with onions, provolone or cheese sauce melted over, piled into long rolls.

Beef chuck and lamb neck browned and simmered with onion, carrot and potato until the potato breaks down, with pickled red cabbage and crusty bread. Brown 600g diced beef chuck and 400g lamb neck in batches. Add 2 sliced onions and 3 carrots in chunks and cook 5 minutes. Add 1kg potatoes in chunks, 1L beef stock and a bay leaf. Simmer gently, partly covered, for 2 hours, stirring now and then, until the potatoes break down and thicken the stew. Season well. Serve with a jar of pickled red cabbage and buttered crusty bread.
W: a box from the Italian bakery near Adrian's

Almond sponge batter split in three, tinted green, left plain and tinted red, baked in thin layers at 175C for 12 minutes, stacked with apricot jam, pressed overnight, covered in dark chocolate and sliced.
K: Training camp honey lemon ginger fizz
between rounds at the training camp

Fresh lemon juice shaken with ginger and honey syrup and a pinch of salt, poured over ice and topped with sparkling water and a lemon wheel. Grate a 4cm knob of ginger into a small pan with 4 tbsp honey and 100ml water and simmer 3 minutes, then strain and cool. Squeeze 3 lemons into a jug, add the ginger syrup and a small pinch of salt and stir. Fill four tall glasses with ice, divide the lemon mix between them and top each with 200ml cold sparkling water. Finish with a lemon wheel.

s.note: the Italian restaurant Rocky runs, named after Adrian
s.how: Fold 150g salami and slices of provolone onto a big board. Warm 200g olives gently in olive oil and spoon over. Add marinated artichoke hearts, strips of roasted red capsicum and torn Italian bread for mopping up the oil.

s.note: the old boxing gym in Philly
s.how: Blitz 250g pitted medjool dates, 100g rolled oats, 3 tbsp peanut butter, 2 tbsp cocoa and a pinch of salt in a food processor until it clumps. Roll into small balls, coat in desiccated coconut and chill for an hour. Fuel for the next round.

m.how: Freeze a 600g rib eye steak for 30 minutes and shave it paper thin. Fry sliced onion and green capsicum on a hot plate until soft, add the beef and sear fast. Lay provolone over the top to melt, then scoop into split long bread rolls.

w.note: a box from the Italian bakery near Adrian's
w.how: Beat 250g almond meal, 4 eggs, 200g sugar and 200g melted butter. Split in three, tint one green and one red, and bake each in a thin layer at 175C for 12 minutes. Stack with apricot jam between, press overnight, spread with melted chocolate and slice.
